title: Account export manifest v1
description:
What one export package says about itself. docs/privacy/PRIVACY_CONTRACT.md#export-privacy is the normative owner, docs/privacy/DATA_MAP.md names the seven domains and owns the Article 20 portability split, packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#exports, #export_artifacts and #export_download_grants are the persistence owners, and the export-job machine owns the lifecycle.

The manifest answers for every domain, included or not. A package that simply omitted a domain was previously indistinguishable from a package that held nothing for it and from one whose producer forgot it existed, because the file list was the only inventory and a file list cannot record an absence. Every exclusion now carries a reason from a closed set, so the participant is told what is not in the package and why, and the completeness check is decidable rather than a count of files.

Nothing here is implemented. No export has been produced, no manifest has been written, and no grant has been issued.

schema_version.description: The manifest format version. A package whose reader cannot tell which format it is holding is a package whose digests mean nothing, because what is digested is decided by the format.

scope.description: The typed scope the participant asked for. It selects which domains are in scope; it never decides on its own that a domain may be silently absent, which is what the domain plan below is for.

snapshot_cutoff_at.description: The single instant every included domain was read as of. One cutoff for the whole package rather than one per domain: two domains read at two instants produce a package whose social edges and whose claims disagree about what existed, and no reader can tell which half is current. docs/privacy/PRIVACY_CONTRACT.md records the export package as the one snapshot-time exception to rechecking authorization at read time, and that exception is only defensible because the subject and the viewer are the same person.

encryption.description: How the package is protected at rest, and under which key. The reference is an identifier and nothing that opens anything: a manifest travels beside the ciphertext it describes, so a manifest that carried what unlocks it would make the encryption a label. The planning validator refuses this schema if it names a property that could hold one.

key_reference.description: An opaque identifier for the key the package was sealed under. It resolves inside the key store and nowhere else.

deletion_state_at_generation.description: The state of this account's deletion job when the package was generated, in the vocabulary the API publishes for it, which is the server-deletion machine less rebuilding-projections. That state is declared internal in docs/architecture/AUTHORITATIVE_STATE_AND_PLATFORM_CONTRACT.md and DeletionJob.state does not carry it; a manifest is handed to the participant, so publishing it here would leak through the package what the API declines to say. It previously carried a fourth spelling of that vocabulary, in which the cooling-off state was snake-cased and the processing and complete states had different words entirely, and no machine, table or API enum used any of the three, so a manifest and the deletion job it described could not be compared at all.

domains.description: One entry per domain in docs/privacy/DATA_MAP.md, always all seven. The planning validator compares this list to the domain enum in packages/schemas/data-disposition-v1.schema.json, so a domain added to the Article 30 record makes every fixture here incomplete rather than leaving the manifest quietly narrower than the record.

data_domain.description: Which domain this file belongs to. A file that belongs to no domain is a file the per-domain counts cannot be checked against.

domain_entry.description: What the package holds for one domain. There is no value meaning "we did not look": a domain that held nothing is `included` with a record count of zero, which is a statement about the account, whereas an enum member for silence would let a package be complete by declining to answer — the same reason packages/schemas/consolidation-plan-v1.schema.json refuses a not-applicable disposition.

record_count.description: How many records of this domain the package holds. Zero on an excluded domain, and zero on an included domain that held nothing.

content_digest.description: The SHA-256 over this domain's records, present exactly when the domain is included. It is what makes a per-domain count checkable rather than asserted: a count with no digest beside it is a number the producer chose.

exclusion_reason.description: Why the domain is absent, present exactly when it is excluded. The set is closed because an open one lets any omission be written into acceptability. `derived-not-portable` is the Article 20 split D-108 records, and a domain excluded for it is still supplied under Article 15 — the manifest says so rather than implying the data does not exist. `rights-of-others` is the Article 20(4) limit. `out-of-scope-for-request` is the participant's own typed scope and is refused when the scope is `all`.

allOf.description: A request for everything cannot exclude a domain for being outside the request. The scope is the participant's own instruction and `all` is the instruction that leaves no domain outside it.
